title: Cadence introduces domain-specialized AI models for chip design
dek: Maestro combines specialized models, agents and EDA tools in a reinforcement-learning loop tailored to design workflows.
evidence: Cadence vendor announcement and early design results
takeaway: Benchmark specialist models on validated task success and end-to-end workflow cost, not token benchmarks alone.

sections.title: Technical approach

bullets.detail: Cadence pairs domain-trained models with its AI Super Agents, EDA/SDA tools and a vertically integrated reinforcement-learning environment.
The design supports cloud and customer-controlled on-premises operation, with some early-access models due in Q4 2026.

paragraphs: Specialization: Cadence pairs domain-trained models with its AI Super Agents, EDA/SDA tools and a vertically integrated reinforcement-learning environment.
Deployment: The design supports cloud and customer-controlled on-premises operation, with some early-access models due in Q4 2026.

sections.title: What to test

bullets.detail: Cadence reports up to 30% higher design quality and up to 5× token efficiency versus general-purpose foundation models in selected workflows; baselines are vendor-selected.
Compare verified design-rule closure, timing/power/area targets, retries and engineer review time under identical design constraints.

paragraphs: Claims: Cadence reports up to 30% higher design quality and up to 5× token efficiency versus general-purpose foundation models in selected workflows; baselines are vendor-selected.
Benchmark: Compare verified design-rule closure, timing/power/area targets, retries and engineer review time under identical design constraints.
